explanations.DB-HIB-001: Retired: without a physical FK, the residual mapped association does not establish a child-side index need. Traversing an owning to-one association loads through the parent's referenced key. Physical FK access-path review remains `DB-SCHEMA-002`; workload-specific child lookup tuning is not inferred.
explanations.DB-HIB-008: Retired: annotation allocation size alone lacks effective optimizer, mismatch strategy, qualified sequence and persistence-unit provenance. Hibernate's documented FIX strategy can override the mapping from the database. Compare effective generator contracts when diagnosing a real mismatch, not coincidentally equal bare names. See the matching [Hibernate 7.4](https://docs.hibernate.org/orm/7.4/javadocs/org/hibernate/id/SequenceMismatchStrategy.html) API.
explanations.DB-SCHEMA-008: Retired: mixed nullability can correctly model a required tenant and an optional relationship. MATCH SIMPLE and MATCH FULL differ; uniform nullability does not establish business intent. Making every column nullable can weaken integrity. See [PostgreSQL foreign keys](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-constraints.html#DDL-CONSTRAINTS-FK).
explanations.DB-SCHEMA-009: Retired: NULLS DISTINCT can be intentional, and Oracle rejects equal non-null portions of partially null composite unique keys, contrary to the previous generalized explanation. See [Oracle integrity semantics](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/cncpt/data-integrity.html).
explanations.HIB-CONFIG-001: **Retired.** Open Session in View is a Spring MVC application setting, not a Hibernate factory option, and the Spring advisor's [SPRING-JPA-001](SPRING-CHECKS.md#spring-jpa-001-review-servlet-open-session-in-view) reviews the same activation with richer registration evidence. Keeping both counted one observation against two advisor scores.
explanations.HIB-ENTITY-002: **Retired.** Hibernate ORM 7 refuses to start an application whose entity declares `@OptimisticLocking(type = DIRTY)` or `ALL` without `@DynamicUpdate` (a `MappingException`, verified on 7.4.5 and 7.4.13, with or without `@Immutable`), so the declaration can never reach the advisor of a running application and the rule could not fire.
explanations.HIB-ENTITY-003: **Retired.** The existence of equality overrides and associations does not show that the methods traverse associations. Safe ID-only implementations also matched. HIB-ENTITY-001 still checks an inconsistent equals/hashCode pair; it does not claim to validate method bodies.
explanations.HIB-ENTITY-004: **Retired.** A toString override plus association declarations does not establish traversal. No method-body analysis proves lazy loading here; safe ID-only implementations must not receive this finding.
explanations.HIB-FETCH-004: **Retired.** Multiple lazy bag declarations are valid; their existence does not establish simultaneous fetching. HIB-QUERY-007 reviews supported query shapes instead. A Java `List` without `@OrderColumn` does not itself prove effective BAG semantics because Hibernate can supply an implicit list index. Changing collections to sets also does not eliminate Cartesian multiplication when multiple collections are fetched together.
explanations.HIB-MAP-012: **Retired.** Jakarta Persistence defines a valid implicit discriminator column. Requiring an explicit annotation solely for visibility scores a supported default without evidence of an incorrect mapping.
explanations.HIB-MAP-017: **Retired.** An owning one-to-one holds the foreign key, so Hibernate can create a proxy without enhancement; the check reported a supported lazy mapping. HIB-MAP-018 covers the inverse side, where enhancement does matter.
explanations.HIB-MAP-019: **Retired.** Annotation declarations cannot verify physical index coverage, and explicit annotation names can still be rewritten by a physical naming strategy. Database structural checks own index evidence; the Hibernate advisor does not duplicate that work by assuming absent `@Index` means absent database index.
explanations.HIB-MAP-021: **Retired.** Hibernate ORM 7.0 removed `@Where` and `@WhereJoinTable`, and every supported runtime uses ORM 7 (Spring Framework 7 requires ORM 7.1 or later; Quarkus 3.40 ships 7.4). Code cannot compile against the removed types, and an annotation whose type is missing at runtime is silently dropped by reflection, so the check could never fire. Migrate any remaining restrictions to `@SQLRestriction`, `@SQLJoinTableRestriction`, or `@SoftDelete` as part of the ORM 7 upgrade.
explanations.MEM-CONTENT-004: Retired: Arrays at 50% or more of shallow bytes is the ordinary shape of a Java heap (compact-string `byte[]`, collection `Object[]`); a healthy JVM sample measured 57%. MEM-CONTENT-001 to 003 remain for big objects, collections, and a dominant non-array class.
explanations.MEM-FOOTPRINT-004: Retired: Host-wide swap is not attributable to this JVM and does not show active paging; macOS dynamic swap files routinely exceed 50% on developer laptops, BootUI's normal context.
explanations.MEM-HEAP-007: Retired: After the histogram request, used heap approximates the live set, and G1's default `MinHeapFreeRatio`/`MaxHeapFreeRatio` (40/70) keep committed heap about 1.7-3.3 times that. Equal `-Xms`/`-Xmx`, which MEM-HEAP-005 and the JVM Tuning calculator produce, always matched. It flagged healthy GC headroom and admitted it was not a sizing recommendation.
explanations.MEM-POOL-006: Retired: Compiler policy, not a memory signal. IntelliJ's Spring Boot launch optimisation adds `-XX:TieredStopAtLevel=1`, so it fired on deliberate development configuration. Real code-cache pressure stays covered by MEM-POOL-002.
explanations.MEM-THREAD-003: Retired: A peak since start or the last reset far above the current count is normal pool elasticity after a burst, not a leak or exhaustion. Current stack reservation stays covered by MEM-FOOTPRINT-002.
explanations.PT-A05-045: Retired: Ordinary caller-known error-path metadata; Boot 4.1 default is always. Never reuse this ID.
explanations.PT-A05-070: Retired: Duplicated QS-CORS-001/002, which always run on Quarkus; delivered CORS stays covered by the synthetic preflight.
explanations.PT-A05-072: Retired: Duplicated QS-TLS-001 at a conflicting severity and ignored the `client-auth=required` default.
explanations.QA-CDI-001: Retired: Framed as a concurrency review prompt, but the real defect on a normal scope is client-proxy field access. Replaced by QA-CDI-004 under a new ID so earlier dismissals of the LOW prompt do not hide the MEDIUM definition error.
explanations.QA-CFG-001: Retired: ConfigMapping is recommended, not mandatory; no custom configuration and programmatic access are valid.
explanations.QA-DB-001: Retired: The finite default maximum is 50; workload/database sizing cannot be inferred from omission.
explanations.QA-PROD-001: Retired: `RUN` can use profile `prod` with Dev Services; the declaration need not be useless.
explanations.QA-PROF-001: Retired: Missing `%prod` keys do not establish missing production configuration.
explanations.QA-RX-001: Retired: JDBC capability plus reactive signatures does not prove an event-loop call; Mutiny offloading is legitimate.
explanations.QA-SCH-001: Retired: Local/per-replica jobs are legitimate; no topology or once-per-cluster intent is observed.
explanations.SPRING-CONFIG-001: Retired: More than 300 bean definitions is not a startup-cost measurement and is exceeded by almost every web, Actuator and data application (BootUI's own beans included). Boot advises against enabling lazy initialization by default because it delays failures and first-request work.
explanations.SPRING-PERF-004: Retired: Property absence cannot establish an unreviewed/undersized pool. Explicitly writing the default 10 changes no runtime behavior; size against database capacity and observed load.
explanations.SPRING-PROFILE-001: Retired: Profiles are optional; configured default profiles and profile-free external configuration are valid.
explanations.SPRING-REACTIVE-002: Retired: A safe bounded default is not a defect, and `spring.codec.*` is stale in Boot 4. The new unlimited-aggregation check addresses a different condition.
explanations.SPRING-WEB-006: Retired: A profile name cannot establish a trusted proxy. Changing header trust needs deployment evidence.
